261	    (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))

So `DivFamZarAff` is the value on which the divisor functor can be a Zariski sheaf over an
ARBITRARY field, with no `|P¹(k)| ≥ n + 2` hypothesis anywhere — the field-uniform fix.

## The two relocated obligations (I-0492 clause 4)

* **(i) fibrewise-finite support.** NOT a field of anything here.  It is not implied by
  what a `LocalEquations` carries (`d.eqn ≡ r` for a non-unit `r ∈ R` is germ-regular with a
  whole fibre curve in its support), so it must come from the seed's own degree data.  It
  enters as an explicit hypothesis at the point of use, never as carrier data: concretely as
  the `hfib` argument of `AffAdaptation.isCertified_of_swallowedBy`
  (`DivisorFamilyAffAssemble.lean`) and as `AffCoverData.SwallowedBy`
  (`DivisorFamilyAffSwallow.lean`).  Neither is a field of anything in this file.
* **(ii) what the fixed-pair confinement was silently supplying.** Discharged in
  `DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean` (`exists_mem_pieces` from the joint cover,
  `flat_sections_pieces` from the flat structure morphism) and in
  `DivisorFamilyAffPerPiece.lean` (the whole per-piece layer, from openness and affineness).

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff` — a certified family over a widened cover.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertifiedAff` — the widened locally-certified predicate.
* `IsLocallyCertifiedAff.of_divEq` — it respects divisor equality.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff` — the widened functor value, with `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`

/-- **The span-`⊤` production rule for local certification.** A local-equation system on
the relative curve is locally certified in degree `n` as soon as, over each member of
some span-`⊤` family of the base, a certified family is divisor-equal to the pulled
system.  This is definitionally `IsLocallyCertified`, exposed as a constructor so that
consumers never unfold the pin — and so that the *localization* step (the only place
where per-piece support isolation is available, `exists_supportTube`) is a licensed
input rather than an obstruction. -/
theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away {n m : ℕ} (g : Fin m → R)
    (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    (hcert : ∀ i : Fin m,
      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (g i)) pi n,
        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))) :
    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n d :=
  ⟨m, g, hg, hcert⟩

        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns

/-- Assemble a divisor-family certificate from finite regular chart colengths and a
submodule which spans the residue-fibre kernels of the Cech difference map.

The overlap product is kept as an explicit finite-flat input: producing it from the
universal seed is part of the geometric base-change wiring, while all consequences for
the certificate are discharged here. -/
theorem isCertified_of_kernel_spanning [IsNoetherianRing R] {n : Nat}
    (hfin : forall j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
    (hregular : forall (j : A.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum R),
      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
        nonZeroDivisors
          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (hovlFinite : Module.Finite R A.ovlProd)
    (hovlFlat : Module.Flat R A.ovlProd)
    (L : Submodule R A.chartProd)
    (hle : L <= LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
    (hspan : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) <=
        LinearMap.range (L.subtype.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (hdim : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
          (LinearMap.ker
            ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) = n) :
    A.IsCertified n := by
  letI hfiniteColength : forall j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := hfin
  letI hprojectiveColength : forall j : A.index, Module.Projective R (A.colength j) :=
    fun j => A.projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j (hregular j)
  letI hflatColength : forall j : A.index, Module.Flat R (A.colength j) :=
    fun j => A.flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j (hregular j)
  letI hfiniteChart : Module.Finite R A.chartProd := Module.Finite.pi
  letI hflatChart : Module.Flat R A.chartProd := Module.Flat.pi_of_finite
  letI hfiniteOvl : Module.Finite R A.ovlProd := hovlFinite
  letI hflatOvl : Module.Flat R A.ovlProd := hovlFlat
  have hfiniteGlued : Module.Finite R A.Glued :=
    Module.Finite.iff_fg.mpr (_root_.IsNoetherian.noetherian A.gluedSubmodule)
  have hprojectiveGlued : Module.Projective R A.Glued :=
    Module.Projective.ker_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le
      (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight) L hle hspan
  refine
    { finite_colength := hfin
      projective_colength := fun j => hprojectiveColength j
      finite_glued := hfiniteGlued
      projective_glued := hprojectiveGlued
      rankAtStalk_glued := fun p =>
        Module.rankAtStalk_ker_eq_of_forall_finrank_eq
          (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight) L hle hspan n hdim p
      flat_coker_incl :=
        Module.Flat.quotient_ker_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le
          (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight) L hle hspan
      flat_coker_diff :=
        Module.Flat.quotient_range_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le
          (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight) L hle hspan }

each chart trace supplies its finite colength, after which

theorem isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning [IsNoetherianRing R] {n : Nat}

      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}

          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
        nonZeroDivisors
          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (hovlFinite : Module.Finite R A.ovlProd)
    (hovlFlat : Module.Flat R A.ovlProd)
    (L : Submodule R A.chartProd)
    (hle : L <= LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
    (hspan : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) <=

11	
12	The corrected cert-collapse claim (roadmap `...certificate.cert-collapse`, as amended after
13	the I-0340 refutation), carried out on the widened cover.
14	
15	## What was refuted and what survives
16	
17	The refuted claim was that (c2)/(c3)/(c4) are FREE for a swallow-or-miss adaptation.  They are
18	not, and `DivisorFamilyAffCollapse.lean` kernel-checks why: `toOvlLeft i i = toOvlRight i i`
19	by `rfl`, so every diagonal component of `deltaLeft - deltaRight` vanishes for EVERY
20	adaptation, and the diagonal factor always survives in the cokernel.  Clause (c4) therefore
21	always implies flatness of the diagonal overlap colengths — no structural observation about
22	which pieces meet the support can remove that.
23	
24	What survives is the REDUCTION the amended node states: on a cover with a straddling piece,
25	(c2)/(c3)/(c4) follow from (c1)-projectivity alone.  This file proves it.
26	
27	## The mechanism, and it is sharper than the node's account
28	
29	With a straddling piece `j₀`, every OTHER piece misses the support, so
30	`subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint` kills every overlap colength that involves an index
31	`≠ j₀` — in particular every OFF-DIAGONAL one, since a pair `(i, j)` with `i ≠ j` has at least
32	one entry `≠ j₀`.  Combined with the vanishing diagonal, `deltaLeft - deltaRight` is the ZERO
33	map (`deltaSub_eq_zero_of_swallowedBy`).  Hence:
34	
35	* `gluedSubmodule = ⊤`, so `Glued ≃ chartProd` — (c2) becomes a statement about the product of
36	  the piece colengths, of which all but one are subsingleton;
37	* `chartProd ⧸ gluedSubmodule` is subsingleton, so (c3) is free — and this IS free, with no
38	  input, which is the one part of the original claim that was right;
39	* `range (deltaLeft - deltaRight) = ⊥`, so the (c4) cokernel is `ovlProd` itself, whose
40	  factors are the overlap colengths: all subsingleton except `ovlColength j₀ j₀`.  So (c4)
41	  reduces to flatness of THAT ONE module — exactly the residue the refutation predicted, now
42	  isolated to a single index instead of a whole cover.
43	
44	## Main declarations
45	
46	* `AffAdaptation.deltaSub_eq_zero_of_swallowedBy` — the difference arrow vanishes identically.
47	* `AffAdaptation.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_swallowedBy` — the equalizer is everything.
48	* `AffAdaptation.gluedEquivChartProd_of_swallowedBy` — hence `Glued ≃ₗ chartProd`.
49	* `AffAdaptation.flat_coker_incl_of_swallowedBy` — clause (c3), unconditionally free.
50	* `AffAdaptation.flat_coker_diff_of_swallowedBy` — clause (c4) from flatness of the single
51	  diagonal overlap colength at the straddling piece.
52	-/

73	/-! ## Every overlap colength off the straddling diagonal vanishes -/
74	
75	/-- **An overlap involving a missing piece has vanishing colength.**  `SwallowedBy` says every
76	piece other than `j₀` is disjoint from the support, and an overlap is contained in each of its
77	two pieces, so it too misses the support. -/
78	lemma subsingleton_ovlColength_of_swallowedBy {j₀ : D.index}
79	    (hmiss : ∀ j : D.index, j ≠ j₀ →
80	      Disjoint d.supportLocus (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))
81	    (i j : D.index) (h : i ≠ j₀ ∨ j ≠ j₀) :
82	    Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
83	  refine A.subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint i j fun z hz hsupp => ?_
84	  rcases h with hi | hj
85	  · exact (Set.disjoint_left.mp (hmiss i hi)) hsupp hz.1
86	  · exact (Set.disjoint_left.mp (hmiss j hj)) hsupp hz.2
87	
88	/-- **The difference arrow is identically zero on a straddling cover.**  On the diagonal it
89	vanishes for every adaptation whatsoever (`deltaSub_apply_diag`, the I-0340 fact); off the
90	diagonal the target is subsingleton, because a pair `(i, j)` with `i ≠ j` has at least one
91	entry different from the straddling index. -/
92	theorem deltaSub_eq_zero_of_swallowedBy (h : D.SwallowedBy d) :
93	    A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight = 0 := by
94	  obtain ⟨j₀, _, hmiss⟩ := h
95	  refine LinearMap.ext fun s => funext fun p => ?_
96	  by_cases hp : p.1 = p.2
97	  · -- diagonal: zero for every adaptation, by proof irrelevance on `inf_le_left/right`
98	    obtain ⟨i, j⟩ := p
99	    cases hp
100	    exact A.deltaSub_apply_diag s i
101	  · -- off-diagonal: at least one index misses the support, so the target is trivial
102	    haveI : Subsingleton (A.ovlColength p.1 p.2) := by
103	      by_cases h1 : p.1 = j₀
104	      · exact A.subsingleton_ovlColength_of_swallowedBy hmiss p.1 p.2
105	          (Or.inr fun h2 => hp (h1.trans h2.symm))
106	      · exact A.subsingleton_ovlColength_of_swallowedBy hmiss p.1 p.2 (Or.inl h1)
107	    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _

111	/-- **The equalizer is everything**: with the difference arrow zero, every section glues. -/
112	theorem gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_swallowedBy (h : D.SwallowedBy d) :
113	    A.gluedSubmodule = ⊤ := by
114	  rw [gluedSubmodule, A.deltaSub_eq_zero_of_swallowedBy h]
115	  exact LinearMap.ker_zero

117	/-- **Hence the glued module is the whole product of piece colengths.**  This is what makes
118	(c2) a statement about the piece colengths — of which, on a straddling cover, all but the
119	swallowing one are subsingleton. -/
120	noncomputable def gluedEquivChartProd_of_swallowedBy (h : D.SwallowedBy d) :
121	    A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.chartProd :=
122	  (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ (A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_swallowedBy h)).trans
123	    Submodule.topEquiv

137	theorem finite_glued_of_swallowedBy (h : D.SwallowedBy d)

139	    Module.Finite R A.Glued := by

146	theorem projective_glued_of_swallowedBy (h : D.SwallowedBy d)

163	/-- The opens-level idempotence, named so the transports below can rewrite with it. -/
164	lemma pieces_inf_self (i : D.index) : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces i = D.pieces i := inf_idem _
165	
166	/-- **The diagonal overlap colength is the piece colength.**  Restriction along
167	`pieces i ⊓ pieces i = pieces i` is an algebra isomorphism carrying the overlap ideal — whose
168	two generators coincide there — onto `span {eqn i}`. -/
169	noncomputable def sectionsInfSelfEquiv (i : D.index) :
170	    Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces i) ≃ₐ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i) where
171	  toFun := relResAlgHom C R (le_of_eq (pieces_inf_self i).symm)
172	  invFun := relResAlgHom C R (le_of_eq (pieces_inf_self i))
173	  left_inv := fun x => by
174	    rw [relResAlgHom_apply, relResAlgHom_apply, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply,
175	      ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
176	    simpa using congrFun (congrArg (fun f => (CommRingCat.Hom.hom f))
177	      (congrArg (relCurve C R).presheaf.map
178	        (congrArg Quiver.Hom.op (Subsingleton.elim _ (homOfLE le_rfl))))) x
179	  right_inv := fun x => by
180	    rw [relResAlgHom_apply, relResAlgHom_apply, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply,
181	      ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
182	    simpa using congrFun (congrArg (fun f => (CommRingCat.Hom.hom f))

185	  map_mul' := map_mul _
186	  map_add' := map_add _

190	lemma sectionsInfSelfEquiv_apply (i : D.index)
191	    (x : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces i)) :
192	    sectionsInfSelfEquiv (C := C) (R := R) (D := D) i x

201	    sectionsInfSelfEquiv (C := C) (R := R) (D := D) i (relResAlgHom C R h x) = x := by

203	    ← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]

210	`pieces i ⊓ pieces i` are the same proof of the same inequality, so the ideal is the span of a
211	single element, and `sectionsInfSelfEquiv` carries it to `span {eqn i}`. -/
212	noncomputable def ovlColengthDiagEquiv (i : D.index) :
213	    A.ovlColength i i ≃ₐ[R] A.colength i :=
214	  Ideal.quotientEquivAlg (A.ovlIdeal i i) (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
215	    (sectionsInfSelfEquiv i)
216	    (by
217	      rw [AffAdaptation.ovlIdeal, Ideal.map_span]
218	      refine congrArg (Ideal.span) ?_
219	      simp)

222	theorem flat_ovlColength_diag_of_flat_colength (i : D.index)
223	    [Module.Flat R (A.colength i)] :
224	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlColength i i) :=
225	  Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv (A.ovlColengthDiagEquiv i).toLinearEquiv
226

233	theorem flat_coker_diff_of_swallowedBy (h : D.SwallowedBy d)
234	    (hdiag : ∀ i j : D.index, Module.Flat R (A.ovlColength i j)) :
235	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)) := by
236	  haveI : ∀ p : D.index × D.index, Module.Flat R (A.ovlColength p.1 p.2) :=
237	    fun p => hdiag p.1 p.2
238	  haveI : Module.Flat R A.ovlProd := Module.Flat.pi_of_finite
239	  have hrange : LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight) = ⊥ := by
240	    rw [A.deltaSub_eq_zero_of_swallowedBy h]; exact LinearMap.range_zero
241	  rw [hrange]
242	  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv (Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot ⊥ rfl)
243	
244	/-! ## The capstone: a certificate from (c1) and the rank alone
245	
246	This is what the reduction is FOR.  `DivisorFamilyAffAssemble.lean`'s
247	`isCertified_of_swallowedBy` had to take (c2)/(c3)/(c4) as hypotheses, because in general
248	they are not free.  On a straddling cover they are not hypotheses at all: they follow from

256	
257	So the corrected cert-collapse claim is discharged: **(c2)/(c3)/(c4) reduce to (c1) plus the

259	theorem isCertified_of_swallowedBy_of_c1 {n : ℕ} (h : D.SwallowedBy d)
260	    (hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
261	    (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))
262	    (hovl : ∀ i j : D.index, Module.Flat R (A.ovlColength i j))
